explanation: Engineer Neil Papworth typed it on a computer and sent it to a Vodafone director's phone during an office Christmas party. Handsets could not yet send texts, so no reply came.

claims.text: The first SMS text message, sent to a mobile phone on 3 December 1992, read 'Merry Christmas'.
The first SMS did not read 'Happy New Year', 'Hello world' or 'Can you hear me?'.
Engineer Neil Papworth sent that message, typing it on a computer.
It was received on the phone of Vodafone director Richard Jarvis, who was at an office Christmas party.
Mobile phones of the time could not send text messages, so Jarvis could not reply.
